shortlist.story: AI analyzed ECG data and identified a previously hidden cardiac signal that predicts a person's risk of sudden cardiac death, according to a new study.
shortlist.best_title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
shortlist.why: Concrete study result; AI is the direct reason the signal was found; high-stakes health finding outside the AI industry; surprising discovery that cardiologists missed it.

shortlist.story: The NHS has begun trialing an AI-powered phone assistant to support patients managing a long-term health condition.
shortlist.best_title: NHS trials AI phone assistant for patients with long-term condition
shortlist.why: Real NHS trial already underway; AI is the reason for the new type of patient support; affects real patients outside the AI industry; in-trial stage with plausible evidence.

shortlist.story: KAIST researchers built a lip-reading AI that achieves a 19.4% word error rate by first identifying clearly readable words and using them as context to decode ambiguous mouth movements.
shortlist.best_title: KAIST develops lip-reading AI that decodes clear words first to resolve ambiguous mouth movements
shortlist.publisher: EurekaAlert / Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
shortlist.why: EurekaAlert lab result with a concrete accuracy metric; real accessibility application for deaf and hard-of-hearing people; AI is the reason accuracy improved; novel technique is surprising.

shortlist.story: A Montreal woman living with ALS used a new AI-powered app to regain a synthesized version of her own voice.
shortlist.best_title: New AI app helps Montreal woman with ALS get her voice back
shortlist.why: Named real person with a result already happening; AI is the direct reason her voice was restored; strong accessibility impact; CBC is an independent credible source.

shortlist.story: A blind veteran from New Orleans used AI-powered smart glasses to navigate independently to a restaurant during a trip to Washington D.C.
shortlist.best_title: Blind New Orleans Veteran Uses AI Glasses To Find His Way To D.C. Pizza Dinner
shortlist.why: Real named person, event already happened; AI glasses are the direct reason he navigated independently; accessibility story with immediate human impact at helping-now stage.

shortlist.story: Researchers developed an AI system that reconstructs the structure of a damaged ship from limited sensor data and rapidly assesses whether it is still seaworthy in an emergency.
shortlist.best_title: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructs Damaged Ships to Rapidly Evaluate Seaworthiness in Emergencies
shortlist.why: Research result with a concrete safety application; AI is the reason rapid assessment from incomplete data is possible; maritime safety outside the AI industry.

shortlist.story: The Society for Neuroscience published findings showing AI tools are already changing how brain scientists analyze data and build computational models of the brain.
shortlist.best_title: Using artificial intelligence to accelerate neuroscience research
shortlist.why: Independent scientific society publishing real findings; AI is the reason research pace and insight have improved; science outside the AI industry is directly benefiting.

shortlist.story: Scientists used an interpretable machine learning model to accurately identify endangered Austrian cattle breeds from their genomic data, a tool that can directly support conservation programs.
shortlist.best_title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accurately Classifies Endangered Austrian Cattle Breeds Using Genomic Markers
shortlist.why: Study result; AI is the reason breeds can be reliably distinguished at scale; conservation and nature application; interpretable model means results are auditable and trustworthy.

shortlist.story: An Arizona judge dismissed a DUI case after finding the police report had been generated by AI, ruling there was insufficient evidence of probable cause.
shortlist.best_title: 'Unable to determine probable cause': Arizona judge releases DUI suspect over AI-generated police report
shortlist.why: System-responding flip: a court acted directly on AI misuse in law enforcement; no one was physically hurt; AI is the reason for both the problem and the judicial response; widely understandable stakes.

shortlist.story: The top scorer on South Korea's national tax examination publicly confessed to cheating with AI, triggering a formal government investigation.
shortlist.best_title: South Korea probes top exam scorer after AI cheating confession
shortlist.why: Owning-up flip: the person responsible confessed publicly and the system is responding with a probe; no physical harm; AI is the reason the cheating was possible; memorable and internationally reported.

shortlist.story: A Japan-led international probe identified roughly 1,000 servers likely used to run AI-driven cyberattacks, demonstrating law enforcement keeping pace with AI-enabled crime.
shortlist.best_title: Japan-led probe finds 1,000 servers likely used for AI-driven cyberattacks
shortlist.why: System-responding flip: international law enforcement exposed AI-enabled attack infrastructure; no one physically hurt; AI is the reason both for the attacks and for the investigation's significance.
